title: Customs Regulatory Authority and Trade Control
summary: This thread covers the foundational legal powers of the government to regulate, prohibit, or restrict the movement of goods across Bangladesh's borders. These powers remain largely static as they form the core legal basis of the Customs Act, 1969.

evolution.legal_basis: Remains consistent as the primary legislative authority for customs control.

timeline.change: Establishment of core sovereign powers to control imports/exports and port clearances.

Customs Act 1969: This act is officially designated as the Customs Act 1969.
The act extends its jurisdiction across the entirety of Bangladesh.
The act shall come into force on a date determined and specified by the government through a notification published in the official gazette.

Customs Act 1969: The Government is empowered under this Act to issue notifications in the official gazette to prohibit or regulate the import and export of specific goods via air, sea, or land routes into or out of Bangladesh.
Import and Export Control: The Government has the authority to restrict or regulate the cross-border movement of specified goods, provided such measures are announced through the official gazette.

member_objects.clause_title: Power to prohibit or restrict importation and exportation of goods
member_objects.resolved_text: 16. Power to prohibit or restrict importation and exportation of goods.- The 2[Government] may, from time to time, by notification in the official Gazette, prohibit or restrict the bringing into or taking out of 3[Bangladesh] of any goods of specified description by air, sea or land.

Government: The Government is empowered to issue notifications in the official Gazette to prohibit or restrict the import or export of specific types of goods.
Importation: The Government has the legal authority to restrict or prohibit the bringing of specific goods into Bangladesh by air, sea, or land.
Export: The Government has the legal authority to restrict or prohibit the taking of specific goods out of Bangladesh by air, sea, or land.
Goods: The Government may regulate the movement of goods into or out of the country by issuing notifications that specify descriptions of goods subject to prohibition or restriction.

member_objects.clause_title: Power to refuse port-clearance to vessels or permission for departure to other conveyance

Port Clearance: The appropriate officer of customs has the authority to refuse port clearance to a vessel or permission for departure to other conveyances until all relevant legal requirements and payments are satisfied.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to demand security, guarantees, or deposits to ensure the payment of dues, taxes, and penalties before granting departure permission to a conveyance.
The officer may require the unloading of goods exported in violation of the law or, if unloading is impractical, demand an undertaking and security for bringing the goods back to Bangladesh.
Conveyance: Departure permission for any conveyance may be withheld until all port dues, charges, and penalties applicable to the conveyance or its person-in-charge have been settled.
Vessel: Port clearance for a vessel may be withheld until all applicable port dues, penalties, and taxes related to the vessel, its master, or its cargo have been paid or secured.
Agent: An agent may provide a written declaration assuming liability for specific penalties and furnish security, thereby becoming responsible for such discharge.
An agent may provide a written declaration assuming responsibility for claims regarding damage or short delivery of imported goods, becoming legally bound to discharge those claims.
Person in Charge: The person-in-charge of a conveyance is responsible for the payment of all dues, taxes, and penalties related to the conveyance or its cargo before departure is permitted.
Export Goods: If export goods are loaded without paying required taxes or duties, or in violation of law, they must be unloaded or the agent must provide an undertaking and security to bring the goods back to Bangladesh.
